title: Are We Addicted to Our Phones?
text:
The average person checks their phone more than eighty times a day. Many of us look at our screens as soon as we wake up and just before we fall asleep. Smartphones are extremely useful; however, a growing number of experts believe they are also changing the way we think and behave.

One problem is concentration. Every time a notification comes up, our attention moves away from what we are doing. As a result, a task that should take twenty minutes can take an hour. Another problem is sleep. The blue light from screens makes it harder for the brain to relax, so people who use their phones in bed often sleep less.

So what can we do? Some people turn off notifications or put their phone in another room while they are working. Others set a daily screen-time limit. For example, a teacher in Ankara asked her students to leave their phones at the door for one week. At first they complained, but by Friday most of them said they felt calmer and had finished their homework faster.
